condition: pediatric acute febrile pharyngitis with rough erythematous chest rash strawberry tongue and 102 F fever in a 7-year-old
level_rationale: Two days of sore throat and 102 F fever followed today by a rough red rash on the chest and a strawberry tongue in a 7-year-old boy describes classic pediatric streptococcal-type febrile pharyngitis with exanthem warranting a same-day outpatient clinic visit for rapid streptococcal testing and oral antibiotic therapy rather than home care alone or emergency care, whereas his throat swelling nearly shut with continuous drooling today signals acute pediatric upper-airway compromise requiring immediate emergency department airway management.
